correctness.rationale: The exact conditional moments for one random attachment yield three first/mixed-moment recurrences. Substitution of the exact degree-profile mean removes the O(1/n) source and gives forcing bounded by n^(-1-delta) uniformly on |z|<=rho<1. The homogeneous product contracts as (j/n)^delta, summing the forcing gives O(n^-delta log n). Cauchy coefficient extraction proves all fixed-degree limits, and deterministic sum_k Y_{n,k}=n gives complementary negative covariance. Independent exact enumeration of (n-1)! recursive trees for each n<=9 verifies the full coefficient vector. Finite checks do not imply the asymptotic theorem; the analytic bound does.

originality.rationale: A new asymptotic covariance of the distinguished root degree with all fixed positive-outdegree counts, plus the noncommuting degree-sum limit, follows from an explicit centered generating-function recurrence. The closest established works give global degree-profile covariances (Janson) and high-degree extreme-value laws (Addario-Berry–Eslava), neither of which directly entails the root/global fixed-degree cross-covariance. The known root/leaf case is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. Relevant older full text was inaccessible, so implicit coverage remains a documented risk.
residual_risks: Historical older joint Pólya-urn methods or Janson full text may implicitly furnish the distinguished-root cross covariance.
Positive limit for fixed outdegrees is a theorem only in the fixed-index regime; it does not identify how the negative compensating coefficient mass migrates to growing outdegrees.

value.rationale: The distinguished root has degree of logarithmic mean while the global outdegree histogram concentrates on small outdegrees. Their O(1) cross-covariance is invisible to leading Gaussian profile limits. The precise positive 2^(-k-1) law for every fixed positive outdegree, simultaneously with exact zero sum over all degrees, identifies a genuine nonuniformity/escape of negative covariance toward growing degree classes and gives sharp, motivated dependence information for recursive-tree network growth.
